cmimc-2022-individual-01.title: Simplify
cmimc-2022-individual-01.body:
$15-213=-198=-6\cdot33$ and $15213=33\cdot461$, so $x=-\frac{461}6\approx-76.83$, whose nearest integer is $-77$.

**Answer: $-77$**

cmimc-2022-individual-02.title: Compare costs
cmimc-2022-individual-02.body:
$40$ single oranges cost $\$40$. $40$ oranges in five-packs is $8$ packs costing $8\cdot4=\$32$. The saving is $40-32=8$.

**Answer: 8**

cmimc-2022-individual-03.title: Percent change of area
cmimc-2022-individual-03.body:
With original side $s$, the new rectangle has sides $\frac65s$ and $\frac45s$, hence area $\frac{24}{25}s^2$. The area changes by $-\frac1{25}=-4\%$, so $k=-4$.

**Answer: $-4$**

cmimc-2022-individual-04.title: List the numbers
cmimc-2022-individual-04.body:
The numbers are $0,\,2,\,20,\,22,\,202,\,220,\,222,\,2022,\,2202,\,2220$ ($10$ numbers: no more than one $0$ and no more than three $2$s). The two middle values are $202$ and $220$, so the median is $\frac{202+220}2=211$.

**Answer: 211**

cmimc-2022-individual-05.title: Extremes of $n$
cmimc-2022-individual-05.body:
If all seven circles are tangent to each other at $P$, there are no other intersection points: $n_{\min}=1$. Any two circles through $P$ meet in at most one more point, and there are $\binom72=21$ pairs, so $n\le1+21=22$, which is attained when no three circles share a second point. The ratio is $22/1=22$.

**Answer: 22**

cmimc-2022-individual-07.title: Periodicity mod 10
cmimc-2022-individual-07.body:
Mod $10$, $9\equiv-1$, so $a_n\equiv2a_{n-1}-a_{n-2}$, which means $a_n-a_{n-1}\equiv a_{n-1}-a_{n-2}$: the sequence is an arithmetic progression mod $10$ with first term $1$ and common difference $0-1=-1$. So $a_n\equiv1-n\pmod{10}$ and $a_{2022}\equiv1-2022=-2021\equiv9\pmod{10}$.

**Answer: 9**

cmimc-2022-individual-08.title: Casework
cmimc-2022-individual-08.body:
If $x\ge1$: $2x-2-2\le x\iff x\le4$. If $x<1$: $2-2x-2\le x\iff-2x\le x\iff x\ge0$. So the solution set is $0\le x\le4$, with minimum $0$ and maximum $4$, sum $4$.

**Answer: 4**

cmimc-2022-individual-09.title: Choose the first two cards
cmimc-2022-individual-09.body:
Given that the third card is $2022$, the first two cards are an unordered pair of distinct numbers from $\{1,\dots,2021\}$, all $\binom{2021}2$ pairs equally likely. The first (smaller) card is $1$ exactly when the pair contains $1$: $2020$ pairs. The probability is $\frac{2020}{\binom{2021}2}=\frac{2020\cdot2}{2021\cdot2020}=\frac2{2021}$.

**Answer: $\frac{2}{2021}$**

cmimc-2022-individual-10.title: Slope of the upper ray
cmimc-2022-individual-10.body:
The top-left vertices of the squares lie on $r_2$. The first two squares are adjacent (the second begins where the first ends), so the left vertices are at heights $20$ and $22$ with horizontal distance $20$ between them: $r_2$ rises $2$ for every $20$ horizontally, a slope of $\frac1{10}$. The third square begins $22$ to the right of the second square's left side, so its height is $22+22\cdot\frac1{10}=\frac{121}5$.

**Answer: $\frac{121}{5}$**

cmimc-2022-individual-11.title: British flag theorem
cmimc-2022-individual-11.body:
For any point $P$ and rectangle $ABCD$, $AP^2+CP^2=BP^2+DP^2$ (drop perpendiculars from $P$ to the sides and use Pythagoras: both sides equal the sum of the squares of the four distances from $P$ to the sides). So $DP^2=400+484-441=443$.

**Answer: 443**

cmimc-2022-individual-12.title: Divisibility by $10^5$
cmimc-2022-individual-12.body:
We need $5^N\equiv5^6\pmod{10^5}$, i.e. $5^6(5^{N-6}-1)$ divisible by $10^5=2^5\cdot5^5$. The factor $5^6$ handles the $5^5$, so we need $32\mid5^{N-6}-1$, i.e. $5^{N-6}\equiv1\pmod{32}$. The powers of $5$ mod $32$ are $5,25,29,17,21,9,13,1$, so the order is $8$ and the smallest $N-6$ is $8$: $N=14$.

**Answer: 14**

cmimc-2022-individual-13.title: Parallelogram law
cmimc-2022-individual-13.body:
Using $|w|^2=w\bar w$: $|z_1+z_2|^2+|z_1-z_2|^2=2|z_1|^2+2|z_2|^2=338$, so $|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=169$. The hypotenuse of the right triangle with legs $|z_1|,|z_2|$ has length $\sqrt{169}=13$.

**Answer: 13**

cmimc-2022-individual-14.title: A recurrence for the distances
cmimc-2022-individual-14.body:
As in the figure, the points $A_1,A_2,\dots$ lie alternately on the two rays. Let $d_k=|A_0A_k|$, so $d_0=0$, $d_1=1$. Take $k\ge1$ and let $M$ be the midpoint of the base $A_{k-1}A_{k+1}$ of the isosceles triangle $A_{k-1}A_kA_{k+1}$ (both legs have length $1$), where $A_{k-1},A_{k+1}$ are on one ray and $A_k$ on the other. Then $A_kM$ is perpendicular to that ray, so $M$ is the projection of $A_k$ onto it and $A_0M=d_k\cos1^\circ$. Hence
$$d_{k+1}+d_{k-1}=2\cos(1^\circ)\,d_k .$$
This recurrence with $d_0=0,\ d_1=1$ has the solution $d_k=\dfrac{\sin(k^\circ)}{\sin(1^\circ)}$, because $\sin((k+1)\theta)+\sin((k-1)\theta)=2\cos\theta\sin(k\theta)$.

The condition $d_i>d_{i-1}$ for $i\le n$ means $\sin(k^\circ)$ is increasing for $k\le n$, which holds exactly up to $k=90$ ($\sin91^\circ=\sin89^\circ<\sin90^\circ$). So the largest possible $n$ is $90$.

**Answer: 90**

cmimc-2022-individual-15.title: Groups
cmimc-2022-individual-15.body:
The sequence is made of groups $1;\ 1,2;\ 1,2,3;\ \dots$; group $k$ has $k$ terms and sum $\binom{k+1}2$. The first $13$ groups contain $\frac{13\cdot14}2=91$ terms, with total sum $\sum_{k=1}^{13}\binom{k+1}2=\binom{15}3=455$ (hockey stick). The remaining $9$ terms are $1,2,\dots,9$ with sum $45$. Total: $455+45=500$.

**Answer: 500**

cmimc-2022-individual-16.title: Levels and linearity of expectation
cmimc-2022-individual-16.body:
Group the vertices by distance from $A$ into four levels: $A$; its $5$ neighbours; their $5$ opposites; $Z$. Moves that never go further from $Z$ never go to a lower level.

- At $A$: every move goes to level 2, so $1$ move.
- At a level-2 vertex: $5$ neighbours; one is $A$ (not allowed), two are in the same level, two in level 3. So $4$ valid moves, $2$ going down. With $E_2$ the expected number of moves to go down: $E_2=\frac12\cdot1+\frac12(E_2+1)$, so $E_2=2$.
- At a level-3 vertex: neighbours are two in level 2 (not allowed), two in level 3, and $Z$: $3$ valid moves, $1$ going down. $E_3=\frac13\cdot1+\frac23(E_3+1)$ gives $E_3=3$.

By linearity of expectation the expected number of moves is $1+2+3=6$.

**Answer: 6**

cmimc-2022-individual-17.title: A line through two points
cmimc-2022-individual-17.body:
$\frac{z-2i}{z+1}$ is real iff $z-2i$ and $z+1$ are real multiples of each other, i.e. $z$ lies on the line through $2i$ and $-1$ (that is, $y=2x+2$ in the plane). The minimum of $|z-1|$ is the distance from the point $1=(1,0)$ to this line: $\frac{|2\cdot1-0+2|}{\sqrt{2^2+1^2}}=\frac4{\sqrt5}$.

**Answer: $\frac{4}{\sqrt5}$**

cmimc-2022-individual-18.title: Volume as a function of $n$
cmimc-2022-individual-18.body:
Each sector has arc length $\frac{2\pi}n$, which becomes the base circumference of a cone with slant height $1$, so its base radius is $\frac1n$ and its height is $\sqrt{1-\frac1{n^2}}=\frac{\sqrt{n^2-1}}n$. One cone has volume $\frac\pi3\cdot\frac1{n^2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{n^2-1}}n$, and the $n$ cones have total volume
$$V(n)=\frac{\pi\sqrt{n^2-1}}{3n^2}.$$
For $n=1$ the cone is flat, $V=0$. For $n\ge2$, $V(n)=\frac\pi3\cdot\frac{\sqrt{n^2-1}}{n^2}$ is decreasing in $n$ (since $\frac{\sqrt{n^2-1}}{n^2}=\sqrt{t-t^2}$ with $t=\frac1{n^2}$, and $t-t^2$ is increasing in $t$ for $t<\frac12$). So the maximum is at $n=2$: $V=\frac{\pi\sqrt3}{12}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\pi\sqrt3}{12}$**

cmimc-2022-individual-19.title: Binomial expansions
cmimc-2022-individual-19.body:
The last term is $(-3)^m\left(-\frac13\right)^n=\pm3^{m-n}$, an integer iff $m\ge n$.

For the first three terms, $(x-3)^m=x^m-3mx^{m-1}+9\binom m2x^{m-2}-\cdots$ and $\left(x-\frac13\right)^n=x^n-\frac n3x^{n-1}+\frac19\binom n2x^{n-2}-\cdots$. The first three coefficients of $P$ are
$$1,\qquad-3m-\frac n3,\qquad \frac19\binom n2+mn+9\binom m2 .$$
The second is an integer iff $3\mid n$. The third is an integer iff $9\mid\binom n2$, i.e. $9\mid n$ or $9\mid n-1$ (since $\binom n2=\frac{n(n-1)}2$ and $\gcd(n,n-1)=1$); together with $3\mid n$ this means $9\mid n$.

So we need $9\mid n$ and $m\ge n$. For $n=9k$ ($k=1,\dots,11$) there are $101-9k$ choices of $m\le100$: $92,83,\dots,2$. The sum is $\frac{11(92+2)}2=517$.

**Answer: 517**

cmimc-2022-individual-20.title: Count the solutions
cmimc-2022-individual-20.body:
**$g^{20}(x)=0$.** For $x\ge20$, $g^{20}(x)=x-20$, so $x=20$; for $x\le-18$, $g^{20}(x)=-x-18$, so $x=-18$. For $-18<x<20$ the values stay integers (solutions must be integers) and $g$ reduces $x$ towards $0$ then alternates $0,1$; parity decides: $g(x)\equiv x+1\pmod2$ so $g^{20}(x)\equiv x\pmod2$, and the iterate ends at $0$ iff $x$ is even. The even integers from $-16$ to $18$ number $18$, plus $x=20$ and $x=-18$: $b=20$.

**$f^{20}(x)=0$.** For $x\ge20$, $f^{20}(x)=x-20$ so $x=20$; for $x\le-20$, $f^{20}(x)=-x-20$ so $x=-20$. For $-20<x<20$ the iterates decrease to $-1$ and then alternate between $-1$ and $0$; again $f(x)\equiv x+1\pmod 2$, so $f^{20}(x)\equiv x\pmod 2$ and $f^{20}(x)=0$ exactly for even $x$ in $(-20,20)$: $19$ values ($-18,\dots,18$), plus $x=\pm20$: $a=21$.

So $a-b=21-20=1$. (A direct computation over all half-integers confirms $a=21$, $b=20$.)

**Answer: 1**
